rules_text:
Rules summary Cards worth points All Aces (A), Kings (K), Queens (Q), Jacks (J), and 10. Special cards Mighty : Ace of spades (unless spades are trumps, then the Ace of diamonds instead). Power: beats anything; you can play it even if it's not the lead suit; if the Ripper requires the Joker to be played and you have the Mighty and the Joker, you can play the Mighty instead. Joker . Power: beats anything except the Mighty; you can play it even if it's not the lead suit since it has no suit. The Joker loses its power if leads the first trick or if the Ripper leads a trick and forces the Joker to be played. Ripper or Joker Hunter : the 3 of clubs (unless clubs are trumps, then the 3 of spades instead). Power: can require the Joker to be played on this trick if the Ripper leads the trick and there cancels the power of the Joker. The Ripper has no effect if it leads the first trick. Variation for 3 players Some cards are removed: 2 to 6 of each suit. The declarer is alone. The bidding starts at 11 points. Joker Hunter is 7 of clubs (if clubs are trumps, then 7 of spades instead).

Other people can raise the bet be in the same suit or on other. Once the bet is settled, the one who won the bet calls for a partner and the round continues - if one side met what they bid, they win points, otherwise, the other side get points, and these (positive and negative) depends on several things. [Rating: 7/10] Point-trick game with initially hidden partnerships. Smoother to learn than Sheepshead because ordering and points for cards are simpler.

[Rating: 7/10] I doubted to buy Mü or try Mighty... I opted for Mighty because Mü is really hard to find, custom deck and therefore harder to get other people playing. Mighty on the other hand can be played with a standard deck, best played with 5, variable partnership, 3 special cards, bidding phase, so really is comparable.   We play it in the office, we either play Tien Len (with 3 or 4) or Tichu and now have Mighty when with 5. So far so good, we enjoy it.

[Rating: 8/10] Other than rummy, the best card game for 5 players. Its rules are a little complicated, especially the first time around, and it takes a good while to learn to bid well, but it always plays very well.

[Rating: 8/10] The best of any pick your partner trick taking games I've played. And much more approachable too, with simpler overall rules and can be played with a standard deck. Not sure if this works at any player count other than 5, but am willing to try at 4 or 6. More or less than that seems untenable.

[Rating: 8.5/10] The best trick-taking game I have learned in a while! best with 5 players. I love the hidden partnership and the fact there is a kitty! The scoring is elegant. This game is my jam and I am excited to play it more. I love having another great card game for 5 players.
